newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX hits yr-high on blue chips gains.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX hits yr-high on blue chips gains.

text.p: The Bratislava Stock Exchange's SAX index hit a year-high on Wednesday, closing up 1.25 points at 203.69 supported by gains to several leading shares.
Steel maker VSZ and and oil refiner Slovnaft led the way higher, rising five and 25 crowns respectively.
But brokers said the bourse has been currently driven up with low volumes in only a few major issues, while the rest of the market is lagging.
"What we see at the moment is Slovnaft and VSZ VZSB.BV acting as the leaders, while the others appear to be losing their breath a bit," Bohus Betko of ING Barings said.

Betko said even though VZS had gained ground, it is one of several cyclical shares that is close to beginning a decline phase. "Looking at the (traded) volumes, I would say orders to buy have dried out," he said.
Drug producer Slovakofarma backed off the 5,000 crown level, closing down 280 at 4,770 crowns, but only six shares traded on the floor.
"It has become clear Slovakofarma will fall the same way it recently climbed -- without volumes," Betko said. "It can loose another 400 crowns very easily."
Overall volume eased to 227,889 shares, from 512,257 shares traded on Tuesday, while turnover decreased to 285.65 million crowns, from 452.52 million.
